Samuel Smith spent years writing songs with a guitar in his hands.

Now, the London-based singer-songwriter is using artificial intelligence tools to help him continue making Americana music after Parkinson's disease largely took away his ability to play guitar.

Smith, who was diagnosed with the progressive neurological disorder in 2020, recently released his second album, “The Art of Letting Go.” For one of the eight tracks, an instrumental piece titled “Horizon,” he relied on platforms that use AI to generate music to create demo arrangements that would convey his vision to the musicians who recorded the song.

The demos he created by humming rough melodies into his phone and uploading the recordings into song generators like Suno and Udio weren't for mixing into the final studio version of “Horizon,” Smith stressed. But tremors, stiffness and fatigue, which are common symptoms of Parkinson’s, caused his guitar skills to deteriorate during the more than a year he worked on the album, he said.

“So then I’m faced with a question,” Smith, 49, said. “‘Don’t play, don’t be creative, or find a way out, find a route.’ And for me, this was the route.”

Generative AI has divided the music industry, whose artists and record labels have complained of their copyrighted work being used to train the models behind AI-powered music tools. Sony Music Entertainment, Universal Music Group and Warner Records sued Suno and Udio in June 2024, although Universal later reached a settlement and partnership deal with Udio and Warner did the same with Suno.

Less discussed is what those platforms can do when employed by a serious musician like Smith, whose disease affects the tools central to his songwriting and identity as a guitarist: his hands. He released his debut album, “In the Springtime,” in 2023, saying he wanted to give his two sons a way to remember when he could perform and record music himself.

“I’d always written, I’d also played, I always sung," he said. "And immediately it became clear to me that I was in trouble, that my music was going to be seriously compromised.”

From prompts to convincing demos

AI music generators use systems trained on large datasets of recorded music and audio. The platforms analyze patterns in melody, harmony, and rhythm before generating new audio based on prompts or uploaded recordings. Users don’t need musical talent to end up with a serviceable song, or even a popular one.

Smith said producing convincing demos from the synthetic tracks the apps generated often required “50, 100, 150 attempts” and extensive editing "to get something that sounds close to my music.” After humming a song into his phone and uploading the recording, he gives prompts describing instrumentation, mood and style. .

“AI is not replacing anything for me,” he said. “It’s unlocking, it’s enabling. It’s allowing me to keep writing. I upload my lyrics; AI doesn’t create my lyrics. I upload my music; AI does not create my music.”

He added: “It then brings it to life in a way that I can play to session players and say, ‘Here, that’s what I’m thinking, that is what I’m hearing.’”

A bittersweet guitar duet

The album was produced by Grammy-winning pianist and producer Matt Rollings, who assembled a group of established roots and bluegrass musicians for the project. They included dobro player and 16-time Grammy winner Jerry Douglas, Grammy-winning banjo player Alison Brown, fiddler Stuart Duncan, guitarist Bryan Sutton, bassist Viktor Krauss and singers Jonatha Brooke and Glen Phillips.

For Smith, the experience of singing in a Nashville studio alongside musicians he had admired for decades was "an extraordinary moment.”

Grammy-nominated guitarist Julian Lage, known for his jazz and acoustic recordings with Blue Note Records, performed on the album’s title track and on “Horizon.” The latter recording became a bittersweet high point in Smith's career; despite the progression of his disease, he managed to play a guitar duet with his friend.

“I hadn’t been able to play for months, but I kept telling myself that if I wrote something to take to the studio, perhaps the clouds would part for a few minutes," Smith said. “That’s what happened. I had a window of about 10 minutes in the studio when my arm freed up. ... So in the end, I was able to capture the last breath of my guitar playing.”

New possibilities and perils

Experts said AI-assisted music tools could benefit other people with disabilities or illnesses.

Ruaidhri Mannion, a composer, music producer and sonic artist who teaches at Brunel University of London, said technology like affordable digital recording software "effectively democratized the making of music” in recent decades. By helping songwriters and musicians communicate ideas and collaborate more easily, AI tools that generate polished-sounding material from voice or text prompts could work in the same way, he said.

“If these tools are able to enable people to be able to participate with other creative groups and encourage more people to feel confident to be able to reach out to an ensemble or an orchestra or something, then I think that is all for the better,” Mannion said.

But an overreliance on technology could intefere with the trial and error, frustration and synergy that are necessary parts of a musician's artistic development, Mannion said.

“What makes a lot of music-making meaningful is the collaborative element,” he said. “There’s a lot of experimentation and development and failure that’s part of musical discovery.”

Udio and Suno have denied copyright infringement allegations and said they wanted to work with the music industry, not in opposition to it. Some musicians are unconvinced. A group of recording artists and activists, including singer-songwriter Tift Merritt, David Lowery of the bands Cracker and Camper Van Beethoven, and ECR Music Group President Blake Morgan, published an open letter in February under the heading “So no to Suno.”

“Many in our community are embracing responsible AI as a tool for creation, and as a means for fans to explore and interact with our artistry. That’s wonderful,” the letter read. “But it’s not the same as creating an environment where AI-generated works sourced from our music are mass distributed to dilute our royalties or, worse yet, reward those actively seeking to commit fraud. Artists need to know the difference.”

‘Show us what you can do’

Smith said he thinks his experience demonstrated how AI could benefit society and expand creative access, if it's developed responsibly.

“My message would be that if these companies want to show they’ve got a place, a role in society, then step up,” Smith said. “Engage with health professionals, engage with music therapists, engage with society and show us what you can do.”

On May 21, Smith collaborated with the Berklee Music and Health Institute for an event in New York that brought together music industry leaders, researchers and clinicians to examine how music can support people living with neurological conditions. Smith discussed his experience living with Parkinson's and sang again alongside musicians who played on “The Art of Letting Go.”

Creating music is crucial to the legacy Smith hopes to leave for his children, ages 4 and 17.

“My 4-year-old is probably never going to remember me playing, and it’s heartbreaking,” he said. “But I’ve been able to pull this into something and refuse to be defined by this disease.”

News.title: Arsenal vs PSG: Your five-minute guide to the Champions League final
News.content:
The Champions League final is the biggest match in club football. This year, Premier League champions Arsenal meet Ligue 1 winners Paris St-Germain. One of them will win a double.

When is the Champions League final?

The match is on Saturday, May 30. Kick-off is at 5pm BST, 6pm in Budapest, where the match is being played.

Uefa, the governing body for the Champions League, changed the start time from the usual 8pm slot in order to increase the broadcast audience. In the Far East, for example, the match will now be shown late at night, rather than in the small hours of the morning.

How to watch the Champions League final on TV in the UK

For the first time since the Champions League format was introduced in 1992, the final is not being shown on free-to-air television in the UK. Instead, it is on TNT Sports. The cheapest option is to take out a month-long subscription to TNT Sports, which costs £30.99 per month.

You can also watch it if you have HBO Max as part of a Sky or Virgin Media TV package or if it is part of your Amazon Prime Video subscription. Alternatively you could watch for £4.99 by subscribing to the HBO Max “Basic with Ads” package and cancelling the subscription within the first month.

News.title: Soccer Aid 2026: When is it, who is playing and how can I watch it?
News.content:
An England XI will once again go head-to-head with a World XI as the 15th edition of Soccer Aid takes place at the London Stadium. Celebrities and footballing legends will take the pitch to raise money for Unicef.

Founded in 2006 by Robbie Williams and Jonathan Wilkes, Soccer Aid has raised over £121m since its inception. England triumphed in 2024 before falling short last year and hope to reclaim the title this year. The head-to-head record stands at eight wins for World XI and six wins for England.

When is Soccer Aid?

Soccer Aid takes place this Sunday, May 31, and kicks off at 6.30pm for viewers in the UK, with coverage starting at 5pm.

Where is it taking place?

The London Stadium, the home of West Ham United, hosts Soccer Aid for the second time. This was the venue for the event in 2022 (a 2-2 draw before the World XI won 4-1 on penalties). For this year’s edition, 60,000 fans are expected to be in attendance.

How can I watch Soccer Aid on TV?

The match will be aired live on ITV1 and STV in the UK and is also available to stream on both ITVX and STV Player.

England squad

Managers: Robbie Williams, Harry Redknapp and David Seaman

News.title: Kenyan court halts US plan to open Ebola quarantine centre
News.content:
A Kenyan high court has temporarily blocked a plan for an American Ebola quarantine centre, hours before the facility had been due to open.

The plan to set up an isolation centre so that United States nationals returning from Congo could quarantine in Kenya rather than in America was opposed by health groups who feared it could import the deadly virus.

A high court judge on Thursday night blocked the centre until a legal challenge could be heard.

Campaign groups have accused the Kenyan government of endangering public health and compromising national sovereignty by agreeing the deal with Washington. The country’s main medical union had also threatened strike action.

“A conservatory order is hereby issued restraining the respondents from establishing... any Ebola exposure, quarantine, isolation or treatment facility in Kenya,” an order from Judge Patricia Nyaundi said. The next hearing is scheduled for June 2.

The outbreak of the rare Bundibugyo Ebola species is tearing through north eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), after apparently having been spreading under the radar for several weeks, if not months.

Since the flare-up was confirmed in ‌mid-May, there have been more than 1,077 suspected ⁠and confirmed cases, including 246 deaths, according to the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC).

News.title: World Cup 2026: Everything you need to know
News.content:
How can I watch the World Cup on television?

BBC Sport and ITV have once again split the matches between them, with two of England’s group matches on ITV (the first against Croatia and third against Panama) and one on BBC (the second match against Ghana). The final will be shown on both channels simultaneously.

Since the 1998 World Cup, England’s win percentage at major tournaments is considerably better on BBC, leading to fears of an “ITV curse”.

Scotland’s group games follow the reverse pattern, with their group-stage opener against Haiti and third match against Brazil on BBC and the middle game against Morocco on ITV.

For the first time, parts of the World Cup will be free to watch on YouTube after Fifa struck an agreement with the streaming platform. The first 10 minutes of every game will be streamed live on YouTube, with broadcasters sharing a select number of full matches on the website. “Content creators” will be part of the coverage as Fifa seeks to attract a new generation of fans.

Fan groups demanded an immediate halt to World Cup ticket sales last December, accusing Fifa of charging “extortionate” prices to the most dedicated supporters.

Football Supporters Europe (FSE), which represents groups across the continent, called for sales via the likes of the Football Association to be suspended when it emerged that watching England at next summer’s tournament could end up costing at least £5,000.

According to FSE, the minimum $6,900 (£5,143) fans would have to pay to follow their country from their first match until the final was nearly five times as much as during the last World Cup.

In response to growing public pressure, Fifa announced a cheaper band of £45 tickets would be made available, but only for a small percentage of seats.

In the latter stages of the tournament, the majority of the cheapest tickets are £686 for the semi-final and £3,119 for the final, pricing condemned by the Football Supporters Association’s Fan Embassy.

“Surprise surprise Fifa are finding out that supporters will turn their backs on ludicrous prices, however prestigious the game. Thousands of pounds for any football match is beyond greedy,” a statement said.

“The most loyal fans, be they English supporters or those of any other nationality, are being priced out.

The final phase of ticket sales will be last-minute general sales, where any remaining tickets are offered on a first-come, first-served basis. This phase will begin in April, and you can access the ticket portal on Fifa’s website here.

There are fears that this World Cup could prove the most expensive ever for supporters, with Fifa operating “dynamic pricing” and taking a 15 per cent fee on resale tickets from both buyer and seller.

News.title: Somalia suffers worst-ever drought – with no aid to help
News.content:
At one point in his life, Abdirahman Mohamed Ali had enough livestock to be considered rich.

Three consecutive failed rainy seasons have taken everything, and all his camels, goats and sheep are now bones on the plains of central Somalia.

“The climate doesn’t have mercy. I’ve been herding livestock for over seventy years and now I’ve lost everything,” he told the Telegraph from his new home in a makeshift tent by a dirt road on the edge of the capital, Mogadishu.

“In the past years, even while herding livestock as they withered away, I would keep going because I knew the rains would come eventually,” the 82-year-old says. “But now it no longer rains.

“When my body began thinning away slowly, was when I realised this way of life was no longer sustainable.

“My health has worsened and I saw all my livestock die,” Mr Ali says.

Somalia is facing its worst drought on record according to the United Nations, and famine is feared to be coming next to the east African nation.

The country faced another terrible drought four years ago, when international aid agencies spent billions trying to stave off starvation.

Yet families arriving at the same distribution points this year have often now found them closed, or empty.

The difference between this year and 2022 is huge international aid cuts, by America, but also by the UK and other European nations.

Somalia’s catastrophic drought risks becoming one of the first major humanitarian crises of the “post-aid era”, the charity Mercy Corps said earlier this month.

The international plan to stave off disaster was only 14 per cent funded by last month. Aid funding in 2022 was $2.4bn (£1.8bn), but by last year had fallen four-fifths to $0.5bn (£0.4bn), in large part because of cuts by the US, which had been the country’s largest donor.

The World Food Programme had aimed to feed two million people this year, but has so far only been able to afford to reach 300,000.

News.title: Katie Boulter becomes fourth Briton to succumb on unlucky court 13 at French Open
News.content:
Katie Boulter became the fourth British casualty of court 13 at Roland Garros, when a three-set defeat by Anastasia Potapova put an end to her hopes in the singles.

Emma Raducanu and Francesca Jones both suffered first set bagels (6-0) and went on to lose on this court, while Cameron Norrie was also on the same patch of clay when he retired in the first round.

Only Jones and Boulter reached the second round out of the six Britons who competed in the first, and neither were able to reach the third, with the latter losing 5-7, 6-4, 6-2.

“Today the match was exactly what I wanted it to be,” Boulter said, after not practising the day before because she was not feeling 100 per cent.

“The result didn’t go my way, but I felt like the type of tennis I was trying to play was miles better than the first round. I think the way that I was aggressive, the way that I struck the ball today, I think was some of the best I have on a clay court.”

Sports.title: World Cup fans could be REFUNDED for tickets with Fifa in legal hot water over ‘illegal price hikes,’ expert warns
Sports.content:
ANGRY soccer fans could get refunded for paying sky-high prices for World Cup tickets, an expert has told The U.S. Sun.

Fifa, soccer’s governing body, has come under mounting scrutiny ahead of this summer’s tournament, which begins on June 11 in Mexico City, over its controversial dynamic pricing ticketing policy.





It’s the first ever World Cup to adopt this sales technique.

New Jersey this week, however, subpoenaed Fifa and demanded a probe into the soaring costs associated with attending matches at MetLife Stadium, which is set to host the World Cup final on July 19.

On Wednesday, New York Attorney General Letitia James and New Jersey counterpart Jennifer Davenport confirmed the launch of joint investigations into the controversy which has cast a dark shadow over the World Cup before a ball has been kicked.

They said in a statement that the ticket prices set by Fifa have “far exceeded the prices for any previous World Cup.”



California’s attorney general has also reportedly written to soccer’s global powerbrokers, questioning whether the ticketing maps told the whole story.

Investigators will examine whether supporters were misled during the sales process for the tournament, which will be staged across the United States, Canada and Mexico.

Fifa has so far declined to comment publicly.

But president Gianni Infantino recently joked that anyone paying eye-watering costs for the final — resale sites were selling spots for $2million — would receive a “hot dog and a Coke,” delivered the by the most powerful man in soccer himself.



Experienced sports lawyer Alexander Rojas said Infantino shouldn’t be smiling, with the investigations carrying significant legal weight.

“State AGs actually have real leverage here,” Rojas explained.

“Fifa is an international governing body, but once it organizes a WC in the US and sells tickets to consumers in the country, it becomes subject to state consumer protection laws like any other business.

“Furthermore, with the World Cup taking place in New York and New Jersey, Fifa can’t ignore any of this.”

The controversy comes as the 2026 World Cup prepares to become the largest ever, expanding from 32 to 48 teams and featuring a record number of matches.



Organizers promoted it as the most accessible edition yet.

But Rojas feels they are liable for serious investigation giving fans, who feel they have been unfairly treated, hope on the horizon.

“Legally, state and local government authorities do control many operational aspects tied to public events,” he continued. “Security and venue compliance, so FIFA cannot completely ignore that factor either.

“Best-case outcome for the AGs is probably some sort of negotiated settlement. That could include refunds, credits, clearer disclosures, inventory releases, or changes to ticket classifications.

“Restructuring seating maps weeks before the tournament would be difficult. I think financial penalties and consumer restitution are much more likely to occur as opposed to an operational disruption.”



Anger has also been sparked about how seating categories were presented during the sales process.

As ticket prices soared, Fifa were accused of shifting seats between pricing tiers after initial purchase phases, with fans allegedly misled about where they would be sitting.

New York Consumer and Worker Protection Commissioner Samuel A. Levine warned that Fifa could face violations of city consumer protection laws if the allegations are proven.

Attorney General Letitia James, meanwhile, said fans should be able to trust that the tickets they purchase match what was originally advertised, adding that consumers should not be pressured into paying excessive prices for seats.

New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill also criticised the situation, saying fans attending matches in the state should not be exposed to unfair or exploitative practices.



Rojas says the situation is “concerning.”

“People bought Category 1 tickets believing they were purchasing the best available seats,” the Miami-based attorney lamented.

“Pushing those seats further back after creating a higher Front Category creates potential deceptive practices and potential misrepresentations.

“Fifa may rely on broad ticketing T&Cs and reservation of rights language, but consumer protection laws can sometimes override boilerplate contract language if AGs believe their conduct was misleading.”

The most likely outcome, according to Rojas, is a negotiated settlement rather than a drawn-out legal battle.



“I do not think this will end in a major courtroom fight,” he said.

“Fifa wants to avoid litigation and bad publicity heading into the WC. The AGs probably want consumer concessions they can present as a win.”

While Fifa later insisted that its seating maps were intended only as a “guidance” tool for fans, members of Congress have also demanded answers.



Congressman Frank Pallone and Nellie Pou raised concerns over what they described as “dynamic pricing rip-offs” and questioned Fifa’s handling of ticket availability

They warned that supply and pricing practices could undermine fairness and transparency.

“The subpoena is less about whether Fifa can charge high prices and more about whether fans were misled during the ticketing process,” added New York attorney Alberto A. Hernandez.

“Dynamic pricing is not automatically illegal, but if consumers were pushed into buying through scarcity that is artificial and shifting rules, that becomes a classic consumer protection problem, not just a sports-business controversy.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Fifa underestimated how politically sensitive World Cup pricing would be in the US markets, especially with rising costs.



“The World Cup is a global event, but it was sold to the US consumer through confusing pricing and seat information. This is a warning to all major sports organizations that premium events do not mean a regulatory free zone.”

Sports.title: ‘Him and Trent shared a Duolingo plan’ – Fans stunned as Anthony Gordon speaks perfect Spanish in Barcelona unveiling
Sports.content:
ANTHONY GORDON has stunned fans with his flawless Spanish during his introduction as a Barcelona player – but he insists he has been prepping for a long time.

The winger has sealed a deal that could be worth over £80 million to the Catalan giants and was introduced to the press on Friday.



Similar to his compatriot Trent Alexander-Arnold when he joined Real Madrid last year, Gordon has impressed with his bilingual abilities.



Gordon said: “Look, believe it or not, I learned Spanish in the past because I’ve always known I would play for Barça… That was my dream.”

“I had a physio at Newcastle, and I always told him that I would play for Barça one day.”

The England international left fans stunned with his fluent Spanish on social media leading to plenty of amusing comments.

Another commented: “You will be busy enjoying a player at your club but that mf is busy learning Spanish to play in laliga.”

A third wrote: “He’s obviously lying… if he went to Madrid he would have said same thing.”

Gordon departs Newcastle after three-and-a-half seasons on Tyneside with a Carabao Cup and two Champions League campaigns to his name.

Sports.title: Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya may never have been in Champions League final without unfortunate red-a*** injury
Sports.content:
DAVID RAYA may not have been in a Champions League final if it was not for an unfortunate red-a*** injury or a National League goalkeeper suffering from Bell’s palsy.

Team-mates, coaches and the man who signed Raya for Brentford tell SunSport his story from over the years…





DANIEL LLOYD-WESTON, Goalkeeper, Southport

“They brought David in after I got Bell’s palsy. He was a young lad, really chirpy, really nice, an enjoyable character to be around. There was no kind of shyness about him.

“He wasn’t overbearing or anything, he was a normal, affable, nice bloke. He came in and he was just brilliant.

“I’m 6ft 1in, he’s shorter than me. Normally when you go further down the leagues, the physicality of the football down that level really is a lot more. Further down the leagues, there’s more physicality. You’ve just got size difference.

“You might not have lads who are the fittest in the world, but they are more than happy to put a foot in.

“David didn’t have that physicality, but what he had was ridiculously good agility. If a cross came in, he would get there before any player.

“I was once told that, because of my height, you’ll never play higher than the bottom end of League One, League Two, at best.

“Yet you look at Raya, who’s only just six foot. He’s that quick and that agile that what he lacks in height, his physical capability makes up for.

“Him coming to Southport was his first taste of men’s football. You’ve got to understand this is a pressure zone now.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“This is where careers live or die and other people’s jobs are on stake down the line. But he took it on so well, he was brilliant.

“He had that temperament while also possessing the physical abilities that he had. Looking at him and judging from the outside, I imagine he could slow time down.”

JOHN KEELEY, goalkeeping coach, Blackburn

“He came up and trained with the first team, we had Paul Robinson there and Jake Kean and Simon Eastwood, Jason Steele.

“As time went by everyone just started going: ‘F***ing hell, he’s decent.’ He just kept getting better and better.



“He got a loan to Southport and I used to go with him. The game that really turned his life around was a Cup game against Derby.

“He had an absolute worldie. When I watched Match of the Day it was unbelievable.

“He never cheated on one thing. He did everything and if he couldn’t do it it’d slowly take the next day to do a bit more. He’s totally dedicated to it.

“I believed straight away he could be Spain’s No1 I wish I’d put a bet on that.

“It was just one thing at a time with him. Then he actually got to play in the first team. We played at Leeds and we trained on Friday morning and we had a bit of a couple of injuries.



“We were warming up and then we were playing two-touch and Simon Eastwood always lost. We played red-a*** for the loser.

“Someone’s tonked it really hard and it hit the back of his hamstring and then it put him out of the game! “Gary Bowyer didn’t want to risk Steele and said let’s play David.

“We didn’t tell him until pre-match. In the first three or four minutes he made an unbelievable save which gave him the confidence. “After four or five minutes in the game he’s now taking free-kicks on the half-way line.

We won, we beat Leeds 4-0 and he carried on playing from there.”



LEE DYKES, Technical director, Brentford

“It wasn’t an obvious deal to do, because you’re always going to look at maybe a lack of height as an issue, which many clubs did.

“Actually, when I was doing the reference check-in from people I knew that worked with him, they also referenced that maybe he could go and play top six LaLiga, but they questioned Premier League potential.

“Whereas our goalkeeper coach, Inaki Cana, who is now at Arsenal, was absolutely drilled down on him being a Premier League player.

“It is how we do things at Brentford, we listen heavily to the specialist.



“We knew what we were signing, but we also knew that height wasn’t an issue because he was so agile and he could jump.

“I am absolutely not surprised and I think he’s one of the best in the world right now.

“He asks questions, he watches footage himself, he analyses his own game.

He’s very critical of himself and just desperate to be the best. That’s not in every player.

“Generally, these types of characters go to the very top. When we signed him, we were signing the potential and we thought we had a really good goalkeeper that could go and play in the Premier League.



“Once he was in the building, we were very sure he would be a Premier League player. Then it was just a case of how high he would go in the Premier League.

“I was surprised that there was only Arsenal at the table when he was clearly available. We had a little bit of a sniff from Tottenham but David made it clear that it was going to be Arsenal.

“There were some complications around the Arsenal deal in terms of they were trying to do it in a certain way. Obviously, it was done initially on a loan because of some financial things on their side.

“Credit to Phil Giles and Matt Benham. They helped David and Arsenal get that deal done. Not many clubs would have allowed a player to go on loan to make the deal happen.

“They waited to see if they could get other interest. I’m sure other interest would have come eventually.



“David Raya, world class, if not the best in the world, big shout for me. A big reason why Arsenal are competing for two massive trophies.

“Arsenal have got a world-class goalkeeper for many, many years to come.”

MARTIN ODEGAARD, captain, Arsenal

“He’s so important for us and it’s great to have a character like him at the back for us as well.

“He’s a leader in the dressing room for sure. He’s a guy who talks a lot and takes a lot of responsibility for the team. He helps me out a lot in terms of being a big part of the leadership group. He’s a great character to have around.



“Everyone can see his quality on the pitch but he brings a lot to the team and to the group. He’s really grown in that role and stature since he arrived here.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“When you look at our team, there are a lot of different leaders, and David is someone who does a lot of work behind the scenes. He talks a lot and he really cares about people and getting the best out of everyone.

“He’s a really big part of the group and a really strong leader.”

Sports.title: Ex-England star Raheem Sterling arrested on suspicion of drug-driving after crashing Lambo on motorway at 9am
Sports.content:
EX-England footie ace Raheem Sterling has been arrested on suspicion of drug-driving after crashing his Lamborghini.

Police pulled over the 31-year-old on the M3 in Hampshire at 9am on Thursday.





Sterling, currently at Dutch side Feyenoord was bailed pending enquiries.

The former Premier League star was arrested on suspicion of drug-driving after crashing his Lamborghini into motorway barriers.

The ex-England, Liverpool and Manchester City winger, 31, had been travelling on the M3 on Thursday morning when the collision occurred.

Police pulled him over on the southbound carriageway in Hampshire at around 9am and arrested him.



Sterling, who was released by Chelsea in ­January before signing for Dutch club Feyenoord, has been struggling, say sources close to the star.

He is suspected of driving a vehicle while unfit through drugs, driving dangerously, possession of a Class C drug, and failing to provide a specimen.

He was released on bail pending further enquiries.

Class C drugs include tranquilisers such as valium, plus steroids, laughing gas and GHB.



Hampshire Police said last night: “Just before 9am on Thursday, we received reports that a Lamborghini was in collision with barriers on the M3 southbound, close to the Minley Interchange.

“No other vehicles were involved and no injuries were reported.

“The driver, a 31-year-old man, from Berkshire, has been arrested on suspicion of driving a vehicle whilst unfit through drugs, driving dangerously, possession of a Class C drug and failing to provide a specimen. He has been bailed while our enquiries continue.”



Sterling was aged just 15 when he was signed by Liverpool from the QPR academy in 2010. He became a fans’ favourite at Anfield before a contract dispute saw him move to Manchester City in 2015.

There he enjoyed massive success — winning four Premier League titles, five Carabao Cups and an FA Cup.

Less successful spells followed at Chelsea and Arsenal, and he moved to Feyenoord as a free agent in February.



Sterling has also won 82 caps for England, scoring 20 goals.

He is engaged to Paige Milian, 30, with whom he has two children.

A source close to him said: “He was a prolific English international who has steered the England squad to significant heights over the last decade and has been made to feel worthless and forgotten about in recent years. The psychological strain that has put on him is immeasurable.”

Sports.title: Haunting reality of Mexico ‘kidnap capital’ hosting World Cup where ‘organ hunters’ roam, kids vanish & tourists killed
Sports.content:
WITH a tear in her eye, Maria Guadalupe Ventura tells me: “The ball is ­coming home, but our missing children aren’t.”

She is one of hundreds of heartbroken mothers who have plastered missing posters on the lampposts outside Mexico City’s Azteca Stadium, where the World Cup kicks off on June 11.





The country will host the tournament alongside Canada and the US, yet for all the excitement here, it is a nation with a dark side.

Most recently, fears are growing of a serial killer on the loose in the resort town of Puerto Vallarta in Jalisco State — an area where multiple games are set to be played — after police discovered the partially dressed bodies of three women, all in their mid-30s.

Drug cartels abduct people at will for organ, sex and human trafficking, and with 130,000 people officially registered missing, the country is nicknamed the “kidnapping ­capital of the world”.

I visited Mexico City to see how dangerous it really is — and what I found was shocking.

Within two minutes of arriving at the Azteca Stadium — where ­Maradona scored his “Hand of God” goal during the 1986 World Cup quarter-final against England — I heard gunshots from the neighbouring area.

While workers were desperately sprucing up the outside of the ­stadium, a block away the streets tell a very different story, with slum housing and a murder rate of 8.6 homicides per 100,000 residents — eight times higher than London’s.

As the shots rang out, an intoxicated security guard, swigging from a Corona bottle, said with a laugh: “Get used to it. It’s Mexico City.”

Another worker added: “This place is like a warzone.”

He was not wrong.





Nearby, a store sells bulletproof vests, not to police or the military but to civilians scared of the gangs.

It is nestled in between a sex shop and a supermarket on a busy main street.

As I enter the premises, owner Edgard Ortiz, 38, hurriedly tells me and my photographer that there is a group outside waiting to rob us and that we must be careful.

There is panic in his eyes.

I then spot a bulletproof vest for a child as young as three among an array of weapons for sale, including a machete. He nods at my look of shock and says: “Anyone can buy these — and they do. They go for about 65 to 105 US dollars.”

The road to the stadium is lined with prostitutes, who stand on the pavements in broad daylight as families walk past.

The women, who are run by the cartel, hustle up business at bus stops, outside restaurants and on the bike path.

Everywhere you look, there are police vans with armed officers, SWAT buses and soldiers carrying machine guns, which they are not shy of using.



As I walked back to my hotel one night, I came across a dead body wrapped in a sleeping bag that had been dumped on a park bench.

Police at the scene told me it was a normal thing to happen and assured me: “Don’t worry, he probably was a bad man.” Amnesty International has called upon Fifa and the World Cup hosts to take urgent action to protect fans.

But just two weeks ago, six men, three women and a child were ­victims of an armed attack at a ­residence in Tehuitzingo, 130 miles from Mexico City.

And last month a gunman killed a Canadian tourist and injured 13 others at Teotihuacan, a popular tourist and archaeological site ­outside the city.

It is a story local mothers know only too well.

Maria, 66, whose 22-year-old son Jonathan has been missing for four years after being snatched by a criminal gang, tells me: “I have no idea where he is, if he’s been put to work or if he’s dead.

“One day he went to the shop and the next he was gone.

“The government only cares about the money the tourists will bring.



“We put these posters up of our loved ones outside the stadium to remind everyone who comes here what is happening, but they keep being taken down.

“I want the world to see them. Mexico City is a very dangerous place. We, the locals, are afraid so you should be, too.”

The Three Lions are scheduled to play at the Azteca Stadium in July if they win their group, and more than 150,000 England fans are expected to descend on the capital.

But Norma Monroy Gracia, 49, whose brother Isaias, 42, has been missing since last year, warns: “Brits beware. Crime is on the rise.

“They need to look out for everything. There is a big problem here with people being taken. And there are two cartels on the highways next to the stadium that take people.

“Tourist destinations are also very dangerous. And taxis can rob them at gunpoint. Things can go very badly for them. Foreign nationals have already been reported missing and many have disappeared and been found dead.

“There is a lack of security and we are a country with many risks.”

Safety questions are still lingering after the killing of a top cartel boss set off widespread violence across the country.



The drug lord, known as El ­Mencho, was shot in a Mexican ­military operation in February.

In response, armed groups unleashed a wave of brutality in 20 states, which prompted talk of the World Cup ­changing venues.

Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum has pledged to bolster ­security, including the deployment of 100,000 National Guard troops, police officers and employees of ­private security firms. But some locals are more worried about the state of the city rather than the violence.

Norma says: “More money needs to be put into fixing the streets.

“They used to prepare for these events but we are just a month away and they are barely fixing anything. They are just painting over the cracks. We are not a suitable country to host these events.”

Some fear the stadium, which is still being renovated, will not be ready in time.

I, too, have some doubts, as I witnessed workers painting walls with a single paintbrush each amid tons of rubble ­surrounding the area.

A punter at the local bar across the street said: “No one thinks it’s going to be ready.



“I hope it is and if it is, please, I’m asking you all to come to ­Mexico. We love to drink beer and so do Brits so we are a match made in heaven.”

That sentiment resonates with the British expats who have moved to the city — and they are not deterred by anything I have described.

Teacher Leo Lawless, 30, from West London, who has been living here since August, says: “I’m so excited for the World Cup.”

Sinking a pint at 10am at The Dog House Pub, he added: “Brits are tough — we aren’t scared of the cartel. I can’t wait for us fans to take over Mexico City.”

Mexico will host 13 World Cup games in total — five in Mexico City, and four each in Monterrey and Guadalajara.

The country will become the first to host the World Cup three times, with the Azteca set to become the first stadium to host the opening match three times.

Security expert Dr Raul Benitez said it is in the best interest of the cartel for ­President Sheinbaum to reach an agreement to prevent Fifa from removing Mexico as a host country.

The cartel wants to avoid a severe government crackdown, and the gangs rely on a stable economy to launder their money through hotels, bars and restaurants.



There was some talk that the football organisation may step in if the country is not able to stabilise — although they have recently said they have “much confidence” in Mexico, despite the cartel violence.

Dr Benitez said: “President Sheinbaum seems very worried because there’s already pressure from the World Cup organisers, and it won’t be long before the United States and President Trump say the same thing. Mexico needs to be at peace for the World Cup to take place.

“Well, that’s the ghost hanging over us now. The government has to pacify the country very quickly.”

There is no pacifying the mothers of the missing, however.

Theresa Guerrero, 59, whose 19-year-old daughter Zaira disappeared in 2011, said: “We are ­suffering in silence.

“All the government cares about is looking good to the rest of the world. Even if our kids are dead, we want the bodies to be able to bury them.”

And as fans arrive to sing in ­support of their teams, the families of the missing have their own chant . . .

“The mothers of Mexico are ­playing the most difficult match: The one for justice.

“Mexico is a champion in ­disappearances.”

Sports.title: Arsenal legends Thierry Henry and Patrick Vieira send secret messages to Gunners squad ahead of Champions League final
Sports.content:
ARSENAL legends Patrick Vieira and Thierry Henry have lifted Mikel Arteta’s stars as they bid to conquer Europe.

The Gunners are aiming to win the Champions League for the first time as they take on Paris Saint-Germain in tonight’s final.





Arsenal, boosted by right-back Jurrien Timber being declared fit, last reached the final 20 years ago – but lost to Barcelona.

Henry was captain that night and has contacted Bukayo Saka, while Invincibles skipper Vieira sent Martin Odegaard a video message.

Arteta has urged his side to take the trophy away from holders PSG in Budapest and Odegaard is motivated by succeeding where previous Arsenal sides failed.

Asked about the message from Vieira, the Gunners skipper said: “It was special.

“He is a proper club legend for everything he’s done. I’ve seen videos and clips, and I’ve heard stories.

“He was such a special leader, that was here at the club. To get a message from him is special.

“Now we have the chance to do something that they haven’t done as well. It’s something nice to play for. We’re just looking forward to the game now. We can’t wait to play.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK



Gunners legend Henry was at the Puskas Arena last night for Arsenal’s open training session and has a strong bond with Saka.

The pair became close following the final of Euro 2020, when Henry reached out to Saka after he missed a penalty in England’s defeat to Italy.

They have stayed in touch ever since and Henry offers words of advice whenever it is required.

Saka last night said: “He messaged me earlier to be fair. He told me he’d see me outside.

“It’s been a consistent theme, he’s been there in the good and bad moments – and I’ve got a lot of love for him and I appreciate him a lot.”



Arteta has not been in touch with Arsene Wenger, who managed Arsenal for their last Champions League final in 2006.

But the Spaniard has been in contact with former players as the Gunners look to land a historic Double after lifting the Prem last week.

Arteta said: “I spoke to a lot of ex-players that are in this position as well, and everybody is rooting for us.

“It’s an opportunity as a club to write something new that we’ve never done. So, that’s what we want to do.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“PSG are defending the trophy, so they were the last ones that had the right to lift that trophy, and they are actually the champions, and we are here to take that away from them.”



Arsenal have a near fully-fit squad for the final. Ben White is out with a knee injury, but fellow right-back Timber is ready to start and play for the first time in two months.

Sports.title: Anthony Gordon COMPLETES stunning £70m Barcelona transfer from Newcastle before jetting off to World Cup with England
Sports.content:
ANTHONY GORDON has completed his £70million Barcelona transfer.

The England winger, 25, departs Newcastle following three-and-a-half years at St James’ Park.





Bayern Munich and Arsenal were also interested in the former Everton ace.

But Barca won the race for his signature after agreeing a deal worth around £70m with Newcastle.

Gordon flew to Spain on Thursday to complete his medical.

The winger subsequently put pen to paper on a five-year contract with Barcelona.

Speaking about the Catalan giants at his official unveiling, Gordon said: “It means everything, to play for Barcelona is the biggest dream possible, it’s the biggest club on the planet, I know it comes with responsibility.

“I’m ready for the challenge. The shirt holds a lot of weight but I’m ready for the challenge.



“I spoke with Hansi Flick, I’m very excited, he’s an amazing man manager, what he’s done for the club is amazing.”

“I was excited to play for Barca when I was three years of age, to play with Lamine (Yamal) and the players is exciting.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“These players are the best players in the world, I seen this at St James’ Park, to do that is really difficult. The fans are also amazing and can create an intense atmosphere but Frenkie and Pedri ruined our plan.

“It’s very special to win anything with Barca, to win here would be special, I want to win every trophy but the Champions League is an amazing trophy.



“To win number six would be an iconic moment and one I would never forget, especially if it happened in my first season.”

Gordon was an unused substitute in Newcastle’s last four matches of the season amid speculation surrounding his future.

His agents Adam Dugdale and Will Salthouse met with Barca sporting director Deco earlier this month ahead of a potential deal.

Bayern had also agreed on personal terms with Gordon.

Barca beat them to the punch, however, by reaching a full agreement with Newcastle first.



And Gordon claims that Barca was always the plan.

He added: “I wanted to speak Spanish because as a kid I believed I would play for Barca. There was a physio in Newcastle and we spoke every day, I told him one day I would play for Barca and wanted to learn Spanish.

“I only won one title with Newcastle, I have a burning desire in my belly, if I had one trophy I’d want to win, it’d be the Champions League.”

On his former club, Gordon told the Toon’s official website: “I owe this club a lot because, when I arrived, I was quite lost both in life and and in football.

“The club has given me a sense of belonging and a sense of identity. It’s allowed me to do what I always thought I could do.



“It’s put me on the biggest stage and allowed me to perform for the shirt.

“Since coming to the club, I feel I’ve improved a lot on the pitch but this club has played a big part in the person I’ve become over the last three-and-a-half years.

“It was really important for me to leave this place in a good way because I’ve loved every single minute of being a part of Newcastle United.

“This is an incredible club and one that I’ll never forget. I’ll be a fan for the rest of my life.”

Gordon’s transfer could leave his England team-mate Marcus Rashford‘s future in limbo.



Rashford impressed on loan from Manchester United but Barca chiefs do not intend to trigger their £26m option to make the deal permanent.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Club bosses have been attempting to settle on a lower fee, but the acquisition of Gordon could see them prioritise other targets.

Barca are said to be plotting a £104m swoop for Atletico Madrid‘s former Manchester City forward Julian Alvarez.

Sports.title: Glam WAGS to fly out early to help England stars relax during World Cup warm-up as Three Lions face hottest contest ever
Sports.content:
WAGS are being drafted in early so England’s stars can chill before the hottest World Cup ever.

Most of the squad fly out to Florida on Monday, before warm-up games in 34C heat and stifling 80 per cent humidity.





And coach Thomas Tuchel has revealed that their partners will be joining them well before the tournament kicks off, in a break from the norm.

He said: “We will go very early to the US, earlier than maybe other teams. We will go there to prepare for the heat and the humidity.

“We will have an early camp that allows us a good mix between free time, family-friends time, and football.”

Bukayo Saka’s fiancee Tolami Benson and Jude Bellingham’s partner Ashlyn Castro are expected to be there, along with Ollie Watkins’ wife Ellie.

Other glamorous guests could include Kobbie Mainoo’s girlfriend Layla Roye, and John Stones’ wife Olivia.

It is unusual for England partners to join the players in a World Cup host country before the tournament starts.



They will be in the US for casual get-togethers after training — with only players and coaching staff allowed in the team hotel.

It is also expected to be more low-key than the Wags’ circus at the Germany 2006 World Cup.



Experts say the tournament in the US, Mexico and Canada, which kicks off on June 11, will be the hottest-ever World Cup — and have warned Fifa of the dangers to players.

Infrared saunas have been installed for months in England stars’ homes to help them acclimatise to the conditions.

Once there, they will be put through gruelling workouts inside heated tents and wear ice vests immediately before games and at half-time.

England’s usual high-tempo game will be impossible, and a different tactic will be required.



Their first warm-up game will be on June 6 against New Zealand at the Raymond James Stadium in Tampa, where 34C is predicted — with some light rain.

And 33C is forecast – but feeling like 40C – in the June 10 friendly with Costa Rica at the Inter&Co Stadium in Orlando.

Kansas City – where England will be based from June 13 – is also forecast to be above 32C.

Footballers can sweat up to five litres – 8.9pints – during games, losing nearly a stone in hot stadiums, analysis shows.



Andrew Simms, director of the New Weather Institute, said: “Player safety is an immediate and urgent concern – things can go wrong very quickly when people overheat.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We’re worried that Fifa is playing recklessly with the health and safety of players.”



Drone flights will be banned above US stadiums hosting World Cup matches as well as over fan events, authorities said.

Sports.content:
Arsenal refused PSG request for Champions League clash with UEFA complaint made

Arsenal and Paris Saint-Germain will do battle in the Champions League final on Saturday evening

View 3 Images PSG weren't happy when they travelled to the Emirates last season (Image: 2025 Jean Catuffe)

Arsenal and Paris Saint-Germain will meet in the Champions League final on Saturday, with their last meeting shrouded in a ticket allocation controversy. Mikel Arteta and Luis Enrique's teams faced each other in the semi-finals of last year's competition.

‌



The French giants won the first leg in north London 1-0. A week later they saw off the Gunners 2-1 to reach the final, where they won the trophy for the first time by thrashing Inter Milan 5-0.

‌



However, mere days before the first-leg semi-final, a speckle of bad blood between the two emerged. Arsenal confirmed that the French champions would be allocated only 2,500 away tickets and not the customary 3,000.

‌



This caught PSG off guard as the Parisians were granted the regular allocation for their league phase fixture at the Emirates earlier in October.

UEFA regulations require clubs to allocate five per cent of a stadium’s capacity to away fans, but 2,500 tickets is closer to four per cent. Arsenal claimed their decision was driven by security concerns and came at the request of local authorities.

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Ibrahima Konate replacement named as Reds 'going all out' for transfer
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Ibrahima Konate replacement named as Reds 'going all out' for transfer

The Liverpool latest sees the Reds eye a replacement for Ibrahima Konate while one star is very much in the club's sights

View 3 Images Konate is set to leave the Reds this summer (Image: Michael Regan/Getty Images)

Liverpool have been rocked by the news that Ibrahima Konate is set to leave the club this summer after failing to agree on a new contract. The French defender has been a key part of Jurgen Klopp and Arne Slot's backline, helping the Reds to several trophies in his time at Anfield, but will now walk away on a free transfer.

‌



The post-season is not even a week old and those Liverpool fans hoping for a peaceful transition from then until the World Cup have met with a rude awakening.

‌



The future of Arne Slot is still an everyday talking point, as is the question of how the club will replace icons such as Mohamed Salah and Andy Robertson. The Konate news has landed like a mean left hook, adding to the Reds' huge to-do list this summer.

‌



The latest news sees Liverpool already in the mix for a replacement for Konate. Elsewhere, the Reds are hoping to land a blow over several of Europe's top teams by going big for a young superstar.

Konate replacement eyed

Liverpool are said to be turning their attention to Juventus' Gleison Bremer in order to replace Konate. According to Calciomercato, the Brazilian centre-back has a big fan in Liverpool's sporting director, Richard Hughes.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Ibrahima Konate set to LEAVE Liverpool after contract talks break down READ MORE :

The Brazilian has emerged as one of Italy's most commanding defenders after joining from Torino in July 2022. It's been reported that the 29-year-old has been put up for sale for around £34.5m.

If Liverpool are looking for a player with strong aerial ability and an eye for goal, then Bremer could be their man. The centre-half scored four times this season and has registered 12 goals in total since joining Juventus.

View 3 Images Gleison Bremer is a reported target for Liverpool (Image: Marco Canoniero/Getty Images)

‌



Konate will be a tough act to follow, however. The 27-year-old will depart Anfield after 183 games, where he won the Premier League title, the FA Cup and the Carabao Cup.

Liverpool going 'all out' for star

Liverpool are said to be determined to land RB Leipzig winger Yan Diomande this summer. The 19-year-old Ivory Coast international has been on the Reds' radar for some time and they are said to be pushing for his signature in the aftermath of Salah's exit from Anfield.

However, the German outfit are said to be demanding around £87m. This week, the Ivory Coast international claimed he’s aware of the interest in him from Liverpool and other elite clubs across Europe.

‌



“Yeah, I heard. But I don’t know if it’s going to be okay for everyone to pay that,” he said, referring to his apparent high asking price. “I’m not going to say Paris, Liverpool or Real [Madrid]. But it would be a good idea to play for big clubs. Everyone has ambitions and every day you want to go higher.”

View 3 Images Yan Diomande could be Liverpool's ideal replacement for Mohamed Salah (Image: Ulrik Pedersen/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Sky Deutschland reports Manchester City and Paris Saint-Germain are in the running to sign Diomande. However, the report says that Reds are ‘going all out’ to bring the attacker to Anfield and want to finalise the signing before the World Cup gets underway on June 11.

Article continues below

That leaves Liverpool with very little time to sort a deal. Another stumbling block is Leipzig's intentions to retain Diomande and extend his contract beyond 2030.

Sports.title: Chelsea's fifth summer signing 'decided' as World Cup star gets Premier League return
Sports.content:
Chelsea's fifth summer signing 'decided' as World Cup star gets Premier League return

Chelsea are reportedly closing in on their fifth summer signing as Xabi Alonso prepares to get to work at Stamford Bridge

View 2 Images Xabi Alonso hasn't even started work at Chelsea but is already homing in on a fifth summer signing (Image: Anadolu, Anadolu via Getty Images)

Xabi Alonso hasn't even taken the reins at Chelsea yet but a roster of new recruits is already taking shape ahead of his arrival. And a fifth signing could be unveiled imminently, with all the signs pointing to it being a question of 'when' rather than 'if'.

‌



In line with the club's commitment to signing young talent under Todd Boehly's ownership, Chelsea confirmed back in January 2025 that Corinthians left-back Denner would be joining on July 1 after he turns 18. The following month brought news of Kazakh teenager Dastan Satpaev before Sporting CP winger Geovany Quenda and Strasbourg forward Emmanuel Emegha were also secured.

‌



Yet Emegha almost certainly won't be the last player to make the journey from Strasbourg to Stamford Bridge this summer. Indeed, the arrival of left-sided specialist Valentin Barco could be made official at any moment.

‌



The Argentina prospect, who has been named in Lionel Scaloni's squad for World Cup 2026, has already confirmed his departure from Chelsea's sister club. And it would appear the former Brighton and Boca Juniors left-back is making the move everyone would expect him to be.

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"Today I say goodbye to this club," the youngster recently wrote on social media in a statement confirming his Strasbourg exit. "I always gave everything on the pitch in every game for this shirt. I want to thank my team-mates, who made everything easier for me.

‌



Xabi Alonso in contact with Real Madrid star who misses Chelsea boss and wanted out READ MORE :

Alejandro Garnacho's Chelsea move goes from bad to worse as dreams crushed after Man Utd exit READ MORE :

"Liam Rosenior and his staff for the confidence they showed in me and for helping shape me as a player; Gary O'Neil and his staff for understanding me and helping me improve; everyone at the club who supports us every day; and the fans for the love they always gave me. Thank you, Strasbourg."

There's a tendency to assume any transfer activity between Chelsea and Strasbourg, or any other club within the BlueCo network, is simply a matter of convenience. Yet that's not the situation with Barco, whose spell in France has seen him emerge as a genuinely exciting prospect.

Reports as early as April suggested the Blues had already reached an agreement with the player ahead of a summer switch. Given this, it remains unclear what has stopped the deal from being confirmed, though it's difficult to imagine significant complications between two clubs under shared ownership.

‌



View 2 Images Former Brighton prospect Valentin Barco appears ready for a Premier League return (Image: Sathire Kelpa/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images)

The 21-year-old landed on French soil in January 2025 (initially on loan from Brighton) as an out-and-out left-back. Plenty of Chelsea supporters might not rate Rosenior's tactical nous particularly highly these days but it was he who first recognised the qualities that could transform Barco - signed by Strasbourg for a mere £8million - into a midfield option.

Positive news for Marc Cucurella, who might otherwise have worried the South American was set to challenge for his position. On that note, however, Barco's arrival would provide much-needed cover at left-back, particularly as Cucurella will soon have just two years remaining on his west London deal and has previously hinted at a potential departure.

‌



Despite standing at a modest 5'6", Barco, now valued at approximately £30m by Transfermarkt, has flourished in his new midfield role. He's demonstrated a knack for pushing forward and creating chances, ending this campaign with nine assists and three goals across all competitions.

Sports.title: Man Utd news: Rafael Leao drops huge transfer hint as 'dream signing' named
Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Rafael Leao drops huge transfer hint as 'dream signing' named

Manchester United's summer transfer prospects are on the up as Michael Carrick goes about improving his options

View 2 Images Rafael Leao has given Manchester United a transfer boost amid speculation he'll be available in a cut-price deal (Image: Piero CRUCIATTI / AFP via Getty Images)

Manchester United have received word off AC Milan forward Rafael Leao that could influence their summer transfer plans. Michael Carrick is currently processing a whirlwind first six months at Old Trafford but has no time to rest on his laurels.

‌



The same can be said for a number of squad stars, many of whom are preparing for the World Cup 2026 kick-off in a fortnight. But with only seven weeks until United's first pre-season friendly, even those with a summer break don't have too long before the action resumes.

‌



That leaves time for a host of new arrivals to plant roots at Old Trafford before Carrick's men reunite in July. And Mirror Football has compiled some of this weekend's top stories as a couple of new names emerge in the rumour mill.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Leao reveals United preference

The Portuguese contingent at Old Trafford could be set to grow by one if United decide to pursue a move for Leao this summer. And they've been encouraged to do after the forward shared his affinity for the club.

The 26-year-old has been linked with United in years gone by without such speculation bearing any fruit. However, the Red Devils may give the idea more thought as Bruno Fernandes and Diogo Dalot could welcome another compatriot to the club.

‌

As a result, it's reported Leao's asking price could be slashed to as little as £43million, which is half the kind of valuations linked to his signature in the past. United's wings aren't believed to be a major priority heading into the transfer window, though Leao has come to be deployed more as a central striker in recent years.

The arrivals of Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo strengthened United's wide areas significantly last summer. That being said, the departures of Marcus Rashford and Alejandro Garnacho mean the left flank in particular could perhaps do with some reinforcement.

United legend Patrice Evra has named Victor Osimhen as the one name he would bring to Old Trafford above all others this summer. Benjamin Sesko demonstrated significant progress over the course of his debut campaign at United but Evra wants to see more striker options at his old club.

‌



Galatasaray spent a Turkish-record fee of around £65m to sign the Nigeria frontman last summer following a successful loan from Napoli. In addition to his supposed £250,000-a-week wages, another obstacle relates to reports that Gala have put a £130m asking price on their star.

Nonetheless, Evra believes his former employers should break the bank to sign one of the hottest finishers in Europe. Doing so would be a move straight from the Sir Alex Ferguson handbook as Carrick looks to fire his team to the next level.

View 2 Images United icon Patrice Evra has recommended his old side sign Victor Osimhen (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"Osimhen. I have all due respect for Galatasaray, the love he gets there and what the player is like," Evra told Goal. "Man United need a proper striker, and I have so much respect for the strikers at Man United, sometimes [Bryan] Mbuemo. But back in the day, we had four amazing strikers, and if you want to play every competition, you need more strikers.

"Of course, you need some defenders, like an extra left-back, because you could have an injury and a right-back. Of course, Casemiro is leaving, so you need to replace those players. To name one player, I say Osimhen because I know these guys can make the difference."

Admittedly, there were portions of last term when United looked light up top, such as when Sesko was injured in late 2025. The likes of Cunha and Mbeumo each had trial runs leading the attack during that period but neither looked a natural fit in the role.

Article continues below

Osimhen helped Galatasaray retain the Super Lig crown this season despite a less prolific campaign by his standards. He finished the campaign with 22 goals and eight assists in 33 games all competitions, having seen his progress impeded by several injury setbacks.

Sports.title: Arsenal vs PSG Champions League Final simulated as EA FC 26 predicts late drama
Sports.content:
Arsenal vs PSG Champions League Final simulated as EA FC 26 predicts late drama

Two newly-crowned domestic champions do battle in this year's Champions League Final, but trying to pick a winner isn't easy work. We took to EA FC 26 to try and predict if Arsenal will finally take the biggest prize in European football.

View 6 Images Arsenal are chasing their first-ever Champions League title, but face tricky opponents in holders PSG (Image: Screenshot/EA Sports)

Arsenal fans have yet to come back to reality after their Premier League campaign ended in glory at long last.

‌



Supporters have been forced to wait a long 22 years between domestic titles, but after three second-place finishes in a row, Arsenal finally got the job done. And yet, this season could still get so much sweeter for the North London side.

‌



The Gunners are chasing an historic double, eyeing a first ever UEFA Champions League trophy. Mikel Arteta's newly-crowned Premier League champions head to the Puskas Arena in Budapest for the club's second-ever Champions League Final.

‌



But 20 years after their last appearance in the European showcase, which they lost to Barcelona in 2006, Arsenal face stiff competition in the competition's current holders. PSG, who are also celebrating domestic success having won Ligue 1 for the fifth time in a row and the 12th time since 2012.

Can Arsenal clinch their first ever Champions League title? Or will PSG solidify their place at the top of the European tree?

We've taken to EA FC 26 to try and give us an idea of what to expect in Budapest.

‌



Arsenal vs PSG score predicted by EA FC 26 simulation

View 6 Images Who will come out on top in Budapest? (Image: Screenshot/EA Sports)

To carry out the sim, we updated the two squads with the latest injury news. That meant Ben White missed out entirely for Arsenal, while doubts like Noni Madueke and PSG's goalkeeper Lucas Chevalier started on the bench.

We predicted Premier League winners Arsenal to line-up in a 4-2-3-1 formation as follows: Raya; Timber, Saliba, Gabriel, Calafiori; Rice, Zubimendi; Saka, Odegaard, Trossard, Gyokeres.

‌



We think PSG will start in a 4-3-3 shape, with the line-up likely to be as follows: Safonov; Hakimi, Marquinhos, Willian Pacho, Nuno Mendes; Zaire-Emery, Vitinha, Joao Neves; Doue, Dembele, Kvaratskhelia.

After all the pomp and ceremony ahead of kick-off, the match that followed continued the recent trend of relatively dull Champions League finals. After PSG romped to a 5-0 victory over Inter last year, the simulated final proved equally as hard to watch but for a very different reason.

View 6 Images Our sim was a tense match where neither team truly threatened to score in 90 minutes (Image: Screenshot/EA Sports)

‌



A terse encounter with timid attacks meant there was only one shot throughout the entire 90 minutes. The only effort came in the form of a wild long-range shot from Jurrien Timber, which was a waste of possession.

Arsenal were in the ascendancy for most of the game, earning 60 per cent of possession, but were unable to create much. Both sides were very poor in the final third, and it took 100 minutes of mind-numbing football for the tie to spark to life.

With the first half of extra time coming to a close, Declan Rice looked in on goal but squared it to Gabriel Martinelli, who had his tame effort stopped by Matvey Safonov. And moments later, we finally had the game's first goal.

‌



View 6 Images Gabriel Martinelli came so close to giving Arsenal the lead in extra time (Image: Screenshot/EA Sports)

With Balon d'Or winner Ousmane Dembele in the clear 12 yards out, David Raya pulled off a crucial save at the near post to deny the French forward on 102 minutes. However, the resulting corner saw the Spanish goalkeeper beaten at the same post.

Dembele's delivery found Joao Neves, who despite his 5ft 9in frame beat both of Arsenal's vaunted centre-backs to the ball. Having somehow won a header against both William Saliba and Gabriel, he directed the ball into the roof of the net beyond a desperate Raya.

‌



View 6 Images How Neves beat both Saliba and Gabriel in the air is a mystery - but it gave PSG a late lead (Image: Screenshot/EA Sports)

Unfortunately for the Gunners, the second half of extra time was more of the same. Arsenal were unable to break down a stout PSG defence, organised superbly by their skipper Marquinhos.

The French side held on to secure back-to-back European titles, and the Brazilian defender lifted the famous trophy after PSG denied Arsenal further glory. Could this win be the sign of a new era of dominance for PSG?

Article continues below

View 6 Images Will this be the closing image of the Champions League campaign? (Image: Screenshot/EA Sports)

Arsenal fans will surely be hoping our EA FC 26 is wrong when the final kicks off at 5pm on Saturday, May 30.

What do you think the final score will be? Let us know in the comments below.

Sports.title: Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal discuss Rashford, Man Utd agree deal, Liverpool exit
Sports.content:
Anthony Gordon says goodbye

Anthony Gordon has uploaded his own personal goodbye to Newcastle United on his social media page. A matter of hours after his move to Barcelona was confirmed, he posted a tribute to his former fan-base.

He said: "To Newcastle. Three and a half seasons have flown by, and it feels like I’ve been here all my life. I arrived as a young boy who had just left home and didn’t know what was to come, but from the very first day I knew I had come to the right place.

"I joined Newcastle because I felt my ambitions matched those of the club, the staff, and the players, and from my first session I knew this was the place I needed to be. To my teammates, staff, and coaching staff, I’m so thankful and grateful that I got to share every day with you all. I wouldn’t be the person or player I am without all of you pushing me each day and the special relationships I’ve been able to build during my time here.

"The Newcastle culture is one of the best there is in terms of discipline, teamwork, and simply being around good people. Every training session and every game in a Newcastle shirt, I knew my team had my back, and I never took that feeling for granted. It’s very rare to find people who want you to succeed as much as you want to yourself, and I felt that every single day. Even in the toughest times, I never took for granted how special it was to come into training every day and be part of this culture and environment.

"To the fans, I arrived in very difficult circumstances, but you still believed in me from day one, and I was determined to prove you all right. From the moment I heard my song at Chelsea, I knew I had to give you all something to cheer for, and I hope you know I gave absolutely everything I had for you and for the club.

"Some of the nights we’ve had at SJP are unforgettable and created some of the best atmospheres I’ve ever witnessed. I hope you get the success you all deserve for the incredible commitment you show in supporting Newcastle, and it has been my pleasure to play in front of you, home and away. "These years have been so successful for both the club and me personally — qualifying for the Champions League two out of three years after being away from the competition for so long, and winning the club’s first trophy in 60 years. I’m so proud to say I’ve been a part of this period in the club’s history."

Sports.title: Ex-England star Raheem Sterling arrested on suspicion of drug-driving after crash
Sports.content:
Ex-England star Raheem Sterling arrested on suspicion of drug-driving after crash

Raheem Sterling has been arrested on suspicion suspicion of driving a vehicle whilst unfit through drugs, driving dangerously, possession of a Class C drug and failing to provide a specimen

View 2 Images Raheem Sterling was most recently with Dutch side Feyenoord (Image: Getty Images)

Ex-Liverpool, Manchester City and Arsenal forward Raheem Sterling has been arrested for driving whilst unfit through drugs after crashing his Lamborghini. Sterling, a 82-time England international, was stopped by police after crashing his car into the motorway barriers on the M3.

‌



A statement from Hampshire Police said on Thursday: “Just before 9am on Thursday, we received reports that a Lamborghini was in collision with barriers on the M3 southbound, close to the Minley Interchange. No other vehicles were involved and no injuries were reported.

‌



“The driver, a 31-year-old man, from Berkshire, has been arrested on suspicion of driving a vehicle whilst unfit through drugs, driving dangerously, possession of a Class C drug and failing to provide a specimen. He has been bailed while our enquiries continue.”

‌



Sterling was eventually released on bail pending further investigation.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Sterling has endured a very difficult few years when it comes to his footballing career. The winger enjoyed a successful period with Liverpool ahead of a move to Manchester City.

‌



He won four Premier League titles during his time at the Etihad Stadium but was sold to Chelsea in 2022. Sterling spent just two seasons at Stamford Bridge before being loaned out to Arsenal where he scored just one goal in 28 appearances.

His remaining contract with Chelsea was ripped up in January, with the wideman then moving to Dutch side Feyenoord.

View 2 Images Sterling endured a difficult spell with Chelsea (Image: Getty Images)

‌



But he made just eight appearances and did not score a goal. Speaking about Sterling after his final appearance for the club, Feyenoord boss Robin van Persie said: "Personally, I struggle with the cynicism surrounding him. think respect is more appropriate. In any case, I don't like cynicism. I can't stand the whole atmosphere around him.

"Everyone has to know their place in that. And I think we sometimes go a bit overboard in the Netherlands regarding that."

"He has scored 200 goals in England and played 82 international matches," Van Persie added. "And that is regardless of whether you think he plays well or not. But I think the way we handle this as a footballing nation is really very bad."

Sports.title: Djokovic sensationally dumped out of French Open by Brazilian teen Fonseca
Sports.content:
Novak Djokovic has been sensationally knocked out of the French Open after losing a five-set epic against 19-year-old Brazilian Joao Fonseca.

The 39-year-old third seed - a big favourite for the title with Carlos Alcaraz injured and Jannik Sinner suffering a surprise defeat on Thursday - flew out to a 5-1 lead in the first set in their third-round encounter, but Fonseca roared back to 5-4 only for Djokovic to keep his composure and serve it out.

A tight second set was pinched by Djokovic 6-4, but his teenage opponent then hit back to win the third 6-3 via some outstanding play.

Fonseca then moved a break ahead in the fourth and consolidated for 2-0, but the Brazilian was broken back when 30-0 up and then missed two further break points at 4-4 in a dramatic game Djokovic survived.

Fonseca kept his head to break the Serbian again at 5-5, however, serving out the fourth set thrillingly to take things to a fifth.

Image: Fonseca played some inspired tennis to beat Djokovic at Roland Garros

After allowing an ailing Djokovic to break him, Fonseca proceeded to come back from 3-1 down in the decider, capping off a sensational 4-6 4-6 6-3 7-5 7-5 victory.

The contest lasted four hours and 53 minutes - the second longest at Roland Garros this year - while temperatures reached 33 degrees.

Image: Djokovic's defeat - from a position of two sets ahead - is a huge shock, and comes a day after Jannik Sinner was knocked out

Djokovic's defeat means the 39-year-old's ‌wait to go past Margaret Court's mark of 24 Grand Slam victories will continue in ⁠the twilight ​of his ​career, and also ​further opens up ⁠the draw in Paris a ⁠day after Sinner's shock exit.

Djokovic, who cut a frustrated figure on Wednesday in his victory over Frenchman Valentin Royer - shushing the crowd, claiming they had 'no respect' and being booed by them - shouted at a camera operator on Friday when two sets up, requesting more space at the change of ends with the camera getting up close and personal.

By contrast, Fonseca was the picture of calm despite his tender years and lack of experience on the professional circuit, remarkably retaining composure and a wonderful ability to strike baseline winners with both forehand and backhand en route to wrapping up a stunning success.

Fonseca: I never believed I could actually win - 'It's crazy'

Fonseca speaking courtside:

"I actually didn't believe I could win the match, I just played and enjoyed being on the court. What an idol we have and what a pleasure it was to step on the court against him - it was my first time - so I thank him, I am very happy.
